paper.journal: Journal of the European Economic Association

prospective establishment status (same / closed / merged / transferred / self-employed / no employees)

variables_mentioned: share of standard tariff contracts in the DA/LO sector

linkages: Workers are matched to establishments through a unique identification number for each individual and establishment, assigned by Statistics Denmark in November of each year
Workers are linked to their unemployment insurance fund (Akasse) through Statistics Denmark information available from 1985 onwards
Each displacement cohort of displaced workers is linked to a comparison group of nondisplaced workers observed over the same six-year window

sample.universe: Workers and establishments in the Danish manufacturing sector covered by IDA between 1980 and 2004; the data source covers a finite period until 2003 for the long-term analyses
sample.unit_of_observation: worker-year (one observation per worker-year in the pooled sample of equation (2)); Tables 3 and 4 use one observation per displaced worker
selection_rules: Mass layoff: a firm's workforce contracts by more than 30% from one observation year to the next
Firms must have at least 50 employees before the mass layoff occurs; closing firms with more than 50 employees are included
Firms that experience a mass layoff but remain in business must have remained the same during the mass layoff period and for at least three preceding observation periods
Firms that experience mass layoffs but do not remain in business must go out of business when the separation takes place and must have remained the same for the three preceding observation periods
Displaced workers: male manufacturing workers, 50 years or younger at displacement, who separate permanently from their establishments
Displaced workers must have at least two years of tenure before displacement and must have been registered as wage employed for 365 days in each of the two predisplacement years
No further restrictions are applied after displacement: displaced workers may be employed, unemployed or out of the labor force

Nondisplaced workers: male manufacturing workers 50 years or younger at the time their counterfactual group is displaced, working for firms with more than 50 employees, never laid off in a mass layoff during the observation period
Nondisplaced workers must have at least three years of tenure and wage employment with a positive income in each subsequent year
Nineteen equidistant overlapping subsamples, one per displacement cohort 1982-2000, each following workers from two years before to three years after displacement
In the pooled sample only one observation per worker-year is kept; for the few workers with more than one displacement within less than four years only the first displacement is taken into account
Hourly wage analyses exclude observations with zero wages and wage observations flagged as poor quality
Tables 3 and 4 restrict the sample to displaced workers with valid wage observations before and after their job loss
sample.period: 1980-2004 (displacement years 1982-2000; long-term analyses use data through 2003)
sample.n_observations: 2,080,471 worker-year observations in the pooled sample (Table B.1); 2,723,280 under the relaxed sample conditions, 1,833,907 in first differences and 159,174 after matching (Table C.1); 294,318-352,623 per equidistant subsample (Tables A.3 and A.4)
sample.n_individuals: Displaced workers per subsample range from 230 ('1984-1989') to 1,038 ('1986-1991'); nondisplaced workers range from 52,699 ('1985-1990') to 61,135 ('1996-2001'); 9,241 displaced workers with valid wage observations in Table 1 and 9,073 in Table 4

construction_notes: Income and labor earnings are deflated and measured in 2000 DKKs; zero income and earnings are included

Hourly wages are total labor income plus mandatory pension fund payments divided by total hours worked in a given year, measured in 2000 DKKs, excluding zero wages; poor-quality wage observations are set to missing
Annual labor earnings are the sum of November job earnings and wages from all other jobs in a given year; if no labor income is reported, earnings are counted as 0
Degree of unemployment is the fraction of a year a worker received UI benefits; UI periods of workers registered as wage employed for the entire year are excluded

Monetary displacement losses are expressed in the figures as a percentage of the base value by dividing the delta^k by the average income, earnings or wages of all displaced workers in the second year before the displacement event
Confidence intervals in the figures are obtained with the delta method

Discounted present values of income losses use a real interest rate of 5% and are normalized by displaced workers' mean income during the baseline period of each sample; losses are not extrapolated beyond the observation period
Displacements occur between November in year (-1) and November in year (0)
Control variables are restricted to five age categories ranging from under 25 to over 55 years, because other observable characteristics are either time constant or endogenous to the displacement
Standard errors are clustered at the individual level
Exports, imports and FDI inflows/outflows are measured in millions of US dollars at current prices and current exchange rates

claims.statement: Among workers displaced before the 1989 decentralization of wage bargaining, displacement changed annual gross income by 2,901.831 DKK in the year before displacement.

treatment.label: Job displacement (separation from the main job during a mass layoff)

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research), Statistics Denmark; the paper names no variable code

definition.value: Indicator D^k_it equal to 1 in the kth year before or after the worker's displacement; a displaced worker is a male manufacturing worker aged 50 or younger who separated permanently from an establishment whose workforce contracted by more than 30% from one observation year to the next (or that closed), the establishment having at least 50 employees before the mass layoff, and who had at least two years of tenure and was registered as wage employed for 365 days in each of the two predisplacement years. Nondisplaced workers have D^k_it = 0 always.

timing.value: Displacements occur between November in year (-1) and November in year (0); the indicator is switched on in the kth year relative to that displacement year.

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research), Statistics Denmark; the paper names no variable code

definition.value: Workers' annual taxable gross income, capturing the entire taxable income including payments from UI or pension funds and other types of income, and including payments from the 'guarantee fund'. Deflated and measured in 2000 DKKs; zero incomes are included.

timing.value: Measured annually; event time runs from two years before to three years after the displacement year.

magnitude.interpretation: In real terms, these income losses correspond to between 0.09% and 0.5% of their average predisplacement income

estimand.target_population: Male manufacturing workers in Denmark aged 50 or younger who were displaced in a mass layoff before the January 1989 wage bargaining reform
estimand.time_horizon: effect measured at event year -1 relative to the displacement year

population.description: Pooled sample containing all individuals of all 19 equidistant subsamples of displaced and nondisplaced male manufacturing workers in Denmark, displacement years 1982-2000; one observation per worker-year.
population.selection: Displaced workers: male manufacturing workers aged 50 or younger at displacement who separated permanently from an establishment during a mass layoff (workforce contraction of more than 30% from one observation year to the next, or establishment closure), in establishments with at least 50 employees before the mass layoff, with at least two years of tenure and registered as wage employed for 365 days in each of the two predisplacement years. Nondisplaced workers: male manufacturing workers aged 50 or younger in firms with more than 50 employees, never laid off in a mass layoff during the observation period, with at least three years of tenure and wage employment with a positive income in each subsequent year.

identification.source_of_variation: The January 1989 renegotiations between DI and CO-metal that decentralized wage bargaining in the Danish manufacturing sector, combined with the timing of mass-layoff displacements before versus after that reform; displaced workers are compared with nondisplaced workers within each period.

key_assumptions.assumption: Parallel trends: in the absence of the displacement, the gross income of displaced workers would have followed the same path as that of the comparison group of nondisplaced workers, within each displacement period.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Footnote 13 names parallel trends as the identification assumption of the difference-in-differences estimators in equations (1) and (2); Figure 4 plots pre-displacement income paths of both groups and Tables A.1-A.2 compare baseline characteristics.

formal.as_written: In contrast to the parallel trends assumption, balanced predisplacement characteristics are not an identiﬁcation assumption of the difference-in-differences estimators in equations (1) and (2).

key_assumptions.assumption: The composition of the group of displaced workers did not change systematically at the reform, so that the post-1989 increase in estimated losses is not a composition effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Figures 2 and 3 show the education and manufacturing-industry composition of displaced and nondisplaced workers over time; the text reports no systematic break immediately after 1989.

key_assumptions.assumption: Macroeconomic conditions and other contemporaneous institutional changes do not account for the post-reform increase in displaced workers' income losses.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table B.1 columns II-V add the national unemployment rate, a Nordic-crisis dummy, FDI flows and exports/imports; Figure 6(b) splits the post-reform period into the 1989-1993 recession and the 1994-2000 recovery; Figures 11 and 12 are placebo analyses for SID workers and the finance sector; Sections 7.2 and 7.3 discuss the 1994 UI reform and the 1992 parental-leave reform.

key_assumptions.assumption: The error term has constant variance and is uncorrelated with the individual and time effects.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated without a test when equation (1) is introduced.

formal.as_written: I assume "it to have constant variance and to be uncorrelated with individual and time effects.

key_assumptions.assumption: Separation from a firm during a mass layoff identifies involuntary job displacement; the paper cannot observe directly whether workers are displaced or leave for other reasons.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Section 3.1 states the measurement problem and imposes establishment-status restrictions from IDA (firm remains the same for at least three preceding periods, or goes out of business) to separate true mass layoffs from workforce transfers and ID changes.

key_assumptions.assumption: No anticipation: workers do not adjust before the displacement year, so the pre-displacement event-time coefficients should be zero.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The model reports the t = -1 coefficient D^{-1}_it; in the pooled pre-decentralization specification of Table B.1 it is positive and significant at the 5% level, and the paper offers no test of no-anticipation.

definition.value: Interaction of the displacement indicator D^k_it with Reform, a dummy equal to one if the worker was displaced after the January 1989 reform that decentralized wage bargaining in the Danish manufacturing sector and zero otherwise. timing.value: Reform is time-constant for almost every displaced worker; the interacted displacement indicator switches on in the kth year relative to the displacement year.

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research), Statistics Denmark; the paper names no variable code

magnitude.interpretation: Income losses of between 6% and 7% of predisplacement income

estimand.target_population: Male manufacturing workers in Denmark aged 50 or younger who were displaced in a mass layoff after the January 1989 wage bargaining reform (relative to those displaced before it)
estimand.time_horizon: effect measured at event year 1 relative to the displacement year

population.description: Pooled sample containing all individuals of all 19 equidistant subsamples of displaced and nondisplaced male manufacturing workers in Denmark, displacement years 1982-2000; one observation per worker-year.
population.selection: Displaced workers: male manufacturing workers aged 50 or younger at displacement who separated permanently from an establishment during a mass layoff (workforce contraction of more than 30% from one observation year to the next, or establishment closure), in establishments with at least 50 employees before the mass layoff, with at least two years of tenure and registered as wage employed for 365 days in each of the two predisplacement years. Nondisplaced workers: male manufacturing workers aged 50 or younger in firms with more than 50 employees, never laid off in a mass layoff during the observation period, with at least three years of tenure and wage employment with a positive income in each subsequent year.

identification.source_of_variation: The January 1989 renegotiations between DI and CO-metal that decentralized wage bargaining in the Danish manufacturing sector, combined with the timing of mass-layoff displacements before versus after that reform; displaced workers are compared with nondisplaced workers within each period.

treatment.label: Displacement after the 1989 decentralization of wage bargaining

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research), Statistics Denmark; the paper names no variable code

definition.value: Comparison of the displacement effect estimated for workers displaced after the January 1989 decentralization of wage bargaining in the Danish manufacturing sector with the displacement effect estimated for workers displaced before it. In the figures this is implemented by estimating the displacement model separately by displacement period (pre-decentralization; post-decentralization recession 1989-1993; post-decentralization recovery 1994-2000) or by interacting the displacement indicators with the reform dummy.

timing.value: Reform date: renegotiations in January 1989 between DI and CO-metal; the post-decentralization period runs 1989-2000.

outcome.label: Largest degree of unemployment reached in the four years after the job loss

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research), Statistics Denmark; the paper names no variable code

definition.value: Fraction of displaced workers whose degree of unemployment never exceeded 20% of a year, or was at least once between 20% and 50%, between 50% and 80%, or larger than 80%, during the first four years after the job loss.

timing.value: First four years after the job loss.

magnitude.interpretation: 0.739 of recession-period displaced workers stayed below 20%, against 0.869 before the reform and 0.841 during the recovery

estimand.target_population: All displaced male manufacturing workers with valid wage observations both before and after their job loss.

population.description: All displaced male manufacturing workers with valid wage observations both before and after their job loss.
subgroups_defined: low predisplacement wage (at or below the median)
population.selection: Displaced workers: male manufacturing workers aged 50 or younger at displacement who separated permanently from an establishment during a mass layoff (workforce contraction of more than 30% from one observation year to the next, or establishment closure), in establishments with at least 50 employees before the mass layoff, with at least two years of tenure and registered as wage employed for 365 days in each of the two predisplacement years. Nondisplaced workers: male manufacturing workers aged 50 or younger in firms with more than 50 employees, never laid off in a mass layoff during the observation period, with at least three years of tenure and wage employment with a positive income in each subsequent year. Table 3 and Table 4 further restrict the sample to displaced workers with valid wage observations both before and after their job loss.

identification.source_of_variation: Comparison of the distribution of displaced workers' largest degree of unemployment across displacement periods.
